title: This 1,000-Year-Old Pine Has Its Own Full-Time Guardian — Huangshan | China Travel Expert
description:
How famous is one tree? China's Guest-Greeting Pine has had its own full-time human guardian for decades — and it's the 19th generation on the job.

The Yingke Song, or Guest-Greeting Pine, clings to a granite cliff on Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) in Anhui, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its sea of clouds and stone peaks. The pine is believed to be over a thousand years old, its two long branches reaching out like arms welcoming guests. A dedicated keeper — currently the 19th-generation guardian — records its temperature, humidity and the state of every needle around the clock, and an alarm system added in 2020 warns when tourists press too close.

🧭 Expert Tip: Take the first cable car of the morning and head straight for the cloud sea — the viewing platforms fill fast, and the clouds usually burn off by late morning.
